summary: Verified Bidar Telethon userbot image-command processing-message deletion bug fix. Ran full pytest suite: 184/184 tests PASSED in 2.10s (0 failures, 0 skips). New regression class TestImageProcessingMessageDeleted (5 tests) all green: cmd_image happy path deletes status message; cmd_image with delete() raising still does NOT relabel a successful send as failed; cmd_imgedit deletes; _do_image_transform deletes; genuine send_file failure still surfaces img_send_failed (delete not called). Manually inspected bidar.py at lines 3045-3069 (cmd_image), 3141-3163 (cmd_imgedit), 3197-3219 (_do_image_transform): each function correctly places send_file in try/except that ends with `return` + finally-unlink, followed by a SEPARATE guarded `try: await msg.delete() except Exception: pass` block. Structural fix matches the described intent. Other message-handling call sites (.up L2568-2575, .say L2308-2320, .sc/music L3463-3482) untouched.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix is correctly implemented and symmetric across all 3 image entry points (cmd_image, cmd_imgedit, _do_image_transform).
bidar.py is ~4305 lines — approaching the 700-line guideline threshold by a wide margin; splitting into modules (image, tts, uploader, music, tldr) would improve maintainability. Not blocking.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bidar is a Telethon userbot (not a web app). Test command: `cd /app/bidar && python -m pytest tests/ -v`. Env vars API_ID/API_HASH/PHONE are stubbed in test file headers. Do not MagicMock telethon.tl.functions.* — breaks import. Current suite: 184 tests, all passing.
rca of the issue: Root cause: In cmd_image / cmd_imgedit / _do_image_transform, `await msg.delete()` was inside the same try block as `client.send_file(...)`. If send succeeded but delete raised (transient/FloodWait), the shared except handler treated it as a send failure — edited msg to 'img_send_failed' and left the processing message in place. Fix (verified): moved msg.delete() out of the send try/except into its own guarded try/except after the send-success path, with the send-failure except carrying an explicit `return` and the finally-block handling temp-file cleanup. Verified by 5 targeted tests + full 184-test regression pass.
